newsitem.title: HONG KONG: China to convene HK 1997 legislature on Jan 25.
newsitem.headline: China to convene HK 1997 legislature on Jan 25.

text.p: China will hold the first formal session of a controversial new Hong Kong lawmaking body later this month in the city of Shenzhen, a Beijing-controlled newspaper reported in Hong Kong on Tuesday.

The 60-member provisional legislature, which will make laws for Hong Kong to take effect after the British colony reverts to Beijing's control on July 1, will meet on January 25, the leftwing daily Ta Kung Pao said.
The session would elect the legislature's president, or speaker, and set the body's rules of procedure, it said.
Britain and Hong Kong's pro-democracy camp have denounced the provisional legislature as a sham. The body was formed in December by a pro-China panel of 400.

Britain has also challenged China to go to the world court to see if the body conforms with handover agreements, while the Democratic Party has branded the legislature illegal and a violation of handover treaties.
China plans to install the body in Hong Kong on July 1 and to dissolve the current legislature which was elected in 1995 for a four year term.
Hong Kong is returning to Chinese sovereignty after a century and a half under the British flag.

Under a 1984 treaty China promised Hong Kong could have a high degree of autonomy and keep its freewheeling capitalist system until 2047, based on Chinese patriarch Deng Xiaoping's policy of "one country two systems".
